findings.explanation: One or more NSExceptionDomains allow cleartext HTTP loads, a TLS version below 1.2, or connections without forward secrecy. MASTG-TEST-0322 and MASTG-TEST-0342 fail on these settings.
findings.remediation: Remove NSExceptionAllowsInsecureHTTPLoads, require NSExceptionMinimumTLSVersion of TLSv1.2 or higher, and keep NSExceptionRequiresForwardSecrecy at its default for each exception domain.
findings.title: ATS exception domains permit cleartext or weak TLS (1)
findings.why: Per-domain ATS exceptions: the hole is real but bounded to the listed hosts.

findings.explanation: The app registers custom URL scheme(s) via CFBundleURLSchemes. findings.explanation: Imports rand() / srand() / random() / drand48(), predictable PRNGs unsuitable for tokens, keys, IVs or nonces. Use SecRandomCopyBytes or arc4random_buf. `arc4random() % n` also introduces modulo bias; prefer arc4random_uniform(n).

findings.explanation: The binary imports dlopen/dlsym, so it can resolve and call code chosen at runtime rather than at link time. That is how optional frameworks, plugin architectures and A/B-tested SDKs are loaded, and it is entirely normal, so this ships as INFO inventory rather than a weakness. It matters only as context: an app that also carries obfuscation (SURV-04) or a data broker (TRK-02) can assemble behaviour a static scan cannot see, and dynamic code loading is the mechanism that makes that possible. Note the limit of the signal: an import proves the symbol is linked, not that it is ever called, and iOS forbids loading code that is not already in the signed bundle. (MASWE-0049)
findings.title: Dynamic loader in use (dlopen / dlsym)

findings.explanation: The bundle references 19 endpoint(s) whose owner is based in US, owners: Apple, Branch, Google, PayPal. findings.explanation: The main Mach-O is encrypted by the App Store. Static string scanning of its TEXT segment won't work without a decrypted dump (e.g., via frida-ios-dump or bagbak on a jailbroken device). Embedded frameworks and dylibs are USUALLY ENCRYPTED TOO (measured 91% across the reference corpus; in half of apps every Mach-O is encrypted), so TEXT-segment string recall is limited bundle-wide, not just for the main binary. What still survives encryption is __LINKEDIT: symbols, imported/defined symbol names, ObjC selectors and linked dylibs, which is why symbol-based detection carries this scan rather than string matching.
findings.remediation: For full TEXT-segment coverage, supply a decrypted .ipa produced by frida-ios-dump or bagbak from a jailbroken device. Resource files, plists, entitlements, symbols, selectors and linked dylibs are still scanned in the meantime.

Its category decides the WP248 criteria: advertising and attribution build marketing profiles (criterion 1) by combining this app's data with what the vendor collects in other companies' apps (criterion 6); session replay observes the person (criterion 3) and profiles usage (1); anti-fraud scores the person (1) to decide whether they may use a service (9); analytics and push engagement profile usage (1); other categories meet none.

permissions.value: This allows you to add Starbucks events to your calendar.
Starbucks can scan some Starbucks Cards to add them to your account
Used to authenticate for reloads and logging in.

permissions.category: Location access while the app is in use
permissions.value: Easily order ahead, get directions and see what's available at nearby stores. Precise location is used to ensure orders are fresh when you arrive.
This allows Starbucks to provide you with a better ads experience.

notes: Main binary is FairPlay-encrypted, TEXT-segment strings are unavailable. Resource files, symbols, and dylibs were still scanned for secrets/endpoints. Drop a decrypted .ipa (frida-ios-dump / bagbak output) for full TEXT coverage.
Code strings are readable in 8 of 55 binaries; 57 rules that search only code strings saw those binaries alone.
No embedded.mobileprovision found, typical for App Store builds re-signed by the store.
